minutes.headline: Board backed fixing the earth removal permit process, and ranked four state budget priorities for FY21.
minutes.summary: The board honored departing state representative Jennifer Benson, heard public comment on the 1325 Mass Ave earth removal project, and appointed members to the Cultural Council and Sewer Commission. It heard the second quarter financial report and ranked projects to send to the state delegation. A long discussion of the earth removal permit that was granted led to a motion to have the land use director or building commissioner available for future permit questions. The board declined to put recreational marijuana prohibition back before voters.

public_comment.topic: Raised health, dust and property-value risks of the 1325 Mass Ave earth removal project and asked the board to convene all key boards.
Sewer Commission vacancies, his stepping down, and a coming sewer rate increase.
Thanked the board for district office space; Lions Club asked about a potato festival on September 19th.
Update on ratifying the patrolman's association contract at town meeting, possibly at a special town meeting.
Abutter described how abutters felt unheard in the earth removal permit hearing.
Questioned whether noise and dust problems were considered, and said the plans keep changing; asked who enforces violations.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to let it question the land-use director or Building Commissioner on project scope during earth removal permitting; the count was not stated.
The board ranked four FY21 state budget priorities: primary school fire alarm, turnout gear, old primary demolition and abatement, then library LED lights.
The board declined to put recreational marijuana prohibition articles back on the warrant or ballot.
The board appointed a Cultural Council member and, jointly with the Sewer Commission, a Sewer Commission member, unanimously.
The finance director reported second-quarter revenues and expenditures on track at the end of December.

why_it_matters: Earth removal permits can affect neighbors through dust, noise and property values, and the vote gives the board a way to get staff answers on scope before it decides on a permit.
Items sent to the state delegation, if funded, could pay for school and town facility needs that would otherwise fall on the local tax bill.
A commissioner said a significant sewer rate increase is likely, which would reach sewer users' bills.
watch_next: How the patrolman's contract is ratified: at annual town meeting or at a special town meeting before it, as the town manager is to work out.
The Lions Club written prospectus for a potato festival, after which the board could meet on next steps.

The key difference is that our minutes list a Cultural Council appointment, a marijuana decision and a potato festival action that the official minutes lack, while the official minutes give vote counts (8-0, 4-1) and a Chairman Alonzo bylaw commitment that ours lack.
